comparison: Both evaluate the Dux-CA system for converting ESCs to 2C-like cells (C3, C40-C45). Both find the methodology robust and well-validated. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative characterization (>60% efficiency, molecular markers), while peer reviewers highlight the system as 'meticulously conducted' and 'a solid resource.' Full agreement on system validity.

Both address heterochromatin reorganization and chromocenter dynamics (C50-C57, C71-C74). OpenEval finds quantitative evidence well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers agree, noting STORM technology provides 'clear and comprehensive insights.' Both accept the morphological observations and measurements without concern.

OpenEval evaluates chromatin decompaction evidence via Voronoi analysis (C58-C63). Peer R2 covers broader heterochromatin dynamics including some overlapping claims (C58, C59, C62). Both support the imaging evidence, with peer reviewers praising the high-resolution visualization approach.

Both address 2C- cell heterogeneity (C60, C61). OpenEval notes the speculation is appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers accept this observation without challenge, recognizing it as descriptive characterization of transition states.

Perfect claim overlap (C64-C70) on 2C-like state exit kinetics. Both find the temporal data well-supported showing rapid transition within 24 hours. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence and correlation of multiple markers. Peer reviewers accept these kinetic observations establishing system reversibility.

OpenEval evaluates chromocenter reformation during 2C exit (C71-C75). Peer R2 includes these claims in broader heterochromatin dynamics assessment. Both support the temporal correlation data and accept the system as modeling developmental chromocenter formation.

Both address chromatin proteomics methodology (C76-C79, C90). OpenEval finds the approach well-validated with appropriate controls and comprehensive profiling. Peer reviewers agree, noting IPOTD 'unveils the chromatome' and provides 'clear and comprehensive insights' as a valuable resource.

Both evaluate proteomic findings on differential protein enrichment (C80-C89). OpenEval supports validation through known markers and novel findings on SUV39H1/H2 patterns. Peer reviewers accept the proteomic data as solid contribution, acknowledging it provides a valuable resource.

Both address protein cluster analysis and TOPBP1 identification (C91-C97). OpenEval finds GO enrichment analysis sound and TOPBP1 focus justified. Peer reviewers accept the identification from proteomic screen, with editor noting 'substantive changes in chromatin association' for TOPBP1.

OpenEval evaluates cluster analysis leading to TOPBP1 (C96, C97). Peer R4 addresses TOPBP1 identification and known functions. Both accept the proteomic identification without challenge, recognizing TOPBP1 as a key candidate from the screen.

Strong overlap on topoisomerase inhibition experiments (C98-C100, C163). OpenEval finds dose-response evidence well-supported with statistical significance. Peer reviewers accept these observations as supporting data, consistent with known topoisomerase effects on cell cycle.

Both evaluate SMARCAD1 localization dynamics (C105-C113). OpenEval finds imaging evidence rigorous with appropriate quantification, noting modest depletion effects. Peer reviewers accept observations but note SMARCAD1 shows 'only modest changes' and request mechanistic studies. Agreement on data, uncertainty on mechanism.

OpenEval addresses SMARCAD1 depletion showing modest effects (C107, C108). Peer R6 questions whether absence of these proteins affects 2C transitions, noting 'major over-arching issue' of function remains unclear. Both recognize limited functional impact in the 2C-like state context.

Perfect claim overlap (C114-C116) on developmental expression patterns from published data. Both accept the scRNA-seq analysis and correlation with chromocenter compaction timing. No concerns raised about this literature-based contextualization.

OpenEval evaluates knockdown experiments on foci maintenance (C117-C122). Peer R6 questions functional significance, noting proteins 'did not affect the entry into or exit from the 2C-like state.' Both recognize the data but peer reviewers emphasize lack of robust mechanistic clarity.

OpenEval addresses parallel knockdown effects (C118-C122). Peer R7 questions the mechanistic relationship, requesting studies on 'how TOPBP1 regulates...SMARCD1.' Both accept morphological observations but peer reviewers find functional conclusions incomplete.

Both evaluate SMARCAD1-TOPBP1 interaction evidence (C123, C124). OpenEval finds co-localization data supportive but notes complex formation is speculative. Peer reviewers agree speculation remains unproven, with editor noting 'conclusions related to functional roles...remain incomplete.'

Perfect claim overlap (C125-C127) on morpholino validation. Both accept these technical observations documenting knockdown efficiency and nuclear localization without challenge. These provide experimental validation for subsequent phenotypic analyses.

OpenEval evaluates SMARCAD1 developmental phenotype (C128-C130). Peer R8 accepts developmental arrest data but notes findings are 'largely descriptive' and requests mechanistic studies on whether chromocenter remodeling directly influences transitions. Agreement on phenotype, uncertainty on mechanism.

Both address TOPBP1 developmental requirement (C131). OpenEval notes complete penetrance and earlier arrest than SMARCAD1. Peer reviewers accept the phenotype but question mechanistic link to heterochromatin maintenance. Agreement on observation, uncertainty on interpretation.

Both evaluate molecular changes in embryos (C132-C134). OpenEval finds temporal data suggesting causal relationships. Peer reviewers accept observations but emphasize descriptive nature and request mechanistic studies. Agreement on data quality, divergence on mechanistic confidence.

Both address synthesis of embryo findings (C135-C137). OpenEval finds functional interaction well-supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers accept developmental arrest but note mechanistic link to heterochromatin 'might contribute' remains speculative and incompletely demonstrated.

Both evaluate methodological contributions (C139, C142, C143, C171). OpenEval finds validation justified and proteomic approach successful. Peer reviewers agree the study provides 'a valuable resource' and 'solid resource to the research community.' Strong agreement on resource value.

OpenEval addresses model system validation (C139). Peer R1 confirms methodology is 'robust' and 'meticulously conducted.' Both agree the reversible system is well-validated for studying chromatin dynamics.

Both contextualize SMARCAD1 findings within ESC literature (C155, C156). OpenEval finds alignment with existing studies appropriate. Peer reviewers accept this contextualization, with Reviewer 1 noting work 'may inform understanding of processes beyond heterochromatin maintenance.'

Both address SMARCAD1-TOPBP1 cooperation parallel to yeast (C161). OpenEval finds comparison reasonable given conservation. Peer reviewers note addition of references on cooperation but editor states 'conclusions related to functional roles...remain incomplete.' Agreement on parallel, uncertainty on mechanism.

Both address topoisomerase/TOPBP1 link to 2C state and development (C163, C164). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by experimental data. Peer reviewers accept topoisomerase inhibition observations as supporting data without challenge.

Both evaluate speculative mechanistic models (C165, C167-C169). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses lack direct experimental support. Peer reviewers agree, explicitly requesting 'mechanistic studies' and noting findings are 'largely descriptive.' Strong agreement that these remain hypothetical.

Both address SMARCAD1 mechanism speculation (C172). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting proposed KAP1-SETDB1 mechanism lacks direct evidence. Peer reviewers agree, requesting mechanistic studies on 'how SMARCD1 associates with H3K9me3.' Both recognize this as unsupported speculation.

OpenEval addresses prolonged 2C program indication (C173) as not robust. Peer R6 questions whether proteins affect 2C transitions. Both recognize limited confidence in functional effects on 2C state dynamics.

OpenEval evaluates 2C+ cell characterization including cell cycle (C46-C48). Peer R11 accepts these cell cycle observations as consistent with previous work. Both support these characterization data without concern.

Peer reviewers accept discussion of published SMARCAD1 findings and alternative mechanisms (C157-C159) without challenge. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these literature discussion claims.
